find: if (host.isSurfaceOpen(surface)) for (const cb of closeCbs) cb();
why: The same leak as the entry above, reached one layer down: the replace path still calls `release()` and the row still exists, but the row does nothing. Worth its own entry because the two are fixed in different places -- a correct replace branch over an empty release row is exactly as leaky as no release at all, and reads more correct. Killed by the pre-existing navigation case as well as the transition one: both drive Customize then `showVersusSetup`, and both read the close count, so an empty row shows up as zero in either. SCOPED TO BOTH FILES deliberately: the leak is asserted in two places -- the navigation case counts the close callback over the gesture, and the transition case reads the same gesture's surfaces -- and naming a killer in a file the entry does not run is a mismatch rather than a claim. Re-pointed in issue #556: the release body moved into `customize-pane.ts` with the rest of the pane, and `hud.ts`'s `LAYERS.customize` row now calls it.
killedBy: createHud application transition contract still RELEASES the replaced pane, which is why the close was not simply dropped
hud: navigation layers -- origin, Back and focus restoration (issue #318) a pane opened while a different pane is up replaces it through that pane's own close, so its close callback fires once
